usageNotes: Use this to enforce backup retention policy on a storage target — it deletes backup files that fall outside the configured keep-* thresholds. Only backups following the standard Proxmox naming scheme (vzdump archives) are evaluated; any non-standard files are ignored. If no prune-backups override is supplied, the retention rules from the storage configuration are used, so verify the storage config before running this in production.

examples.summary: Prune backups for a single VM (ID 101) on local backup storage, keeping only the last 3 backups

destructiveReason: Permanently deletes backup files from storage that do not satisfy the retention policy; deleted backups cannot be recovered.
tips: Run GET /nodes/{node}/storage/{storage}/prunebackups first (dry-run) to preview which backups would be removed before committing the DELETE.
Omitting 'vmid' and 'type' prunes backups for ALL guests on the storage — scope carefully in mixed environments.
The 'prune-backups' override only applies to this single call; it does not permanently change the storage retention configuration.
Requires 'Datastore.Allocate' on the storage path; if scoped to a specific VMID, 'Datastore.AllocateSpace' + 'VM.Backup' on that VM are sufficient.
The operation returns a string (task UPID) — poll /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to confirm completion before assuming backups are gone.
